property_summary: For any admissible input, transfer must return true when all internal transferFrom calls succeed; the mutated version returns false instead.
For any admissible input where the internal calls to transferFrom all succeed, the transfer function must return true; the bug returns false instead.
For any non-empty recipient array, the reference transfer succeeds and returns true, while the mutant always reverts due to a reversed length check.

The reference contract always succeeds on every element of _tos, so the entire transfer call never reverts; the mutant drops the require, making failed sub-calls invisible and the overall call succeeds when the reference would revert.

The reference contract always emits a call using the 'transferFrom' selector, whereas the mutant uses 'transfer', causing a different external call; the rule is that a successful transfer call to a contract that reverts on the fallback function should succeed in the reference but revert in the mutant when the called contract distinguishes selectors by reverting on unknown selectors.
For a callee that implements a fallback reverting on unknown selectors, the reference call succeeds while the mutant reverts because it uses a different function selector.

For every external call made by c.transfer, the callee receives the transferFrom selector; the mutant sends a transfer selector, so a callee that only accepts transferFrom will revert only under the mutant.

The contract should attempt a transfer for every recipient in the _tos array; the mutant skips the first recipient, so if there is exactly one recipient no external call is made and transfer still returns true, while the reference makes one call.
